summary.intent: Get started on the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony's launch: analyze the supplier data, then build a product (poller, extraction/recheck-and-act agents, routines, calm phone-first UI) that finds hidden launch risks and acts on them.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the portal data and found the Collector's Edition and game-card shortfalls the plan hid. Built a versioned poller, agents, routines backend, verifier shortfall fix (34,800 to 6,800), the calm 'Today' UI and an email-review-before-send step; briefing page, interview doc and design canvas published, work committed locally but not pushed.

repo: Portal API has only /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip; no webhooks or notifications. The only way to detect changes is polling the list and comparing SHA-256, and files get replaced under the same name.
data/ (raw portal data, notes, scans, designs) and .env are gitignored because the data is confidential; only .env.example is committed.
The team workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; claim a task with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md before building.
Entire hooks only create a checkpoint when repo files change; 'no files modified during session, skipping checkpoint' is normal for read-only turns.

The verifier counts inbound deliveries only if the supplier shipping document confirms them. Unread documents are conservatively not counted, so the card gap showed 34,800 until the Hwaseong shipping advice was read by the image recognizer.
The image recognizer put the part number in the `item` field with an empty `material_id`; the linker needed a part-number fallback to recognize the short shipment.

Data traps found: art book receipt booked 80,000 vs 8,000 delivered; 5,600 failed statues booked as unrestricted; sleeve artwork rev B vs rev C; Boise delivers EXW not DDP; lid magnets are fitted by PackRight so the BOM line is a false alarm.
Backend routines: four triggers (decisions, waiting, replies, shipments), steps send/chase/call/ask_status, trust modes ask/tell/quiet, undo that refuses once an email or call has gone out.

code.finding: Parts now carry `arriving` and `not_counted` lists, and gap = needed - usable - arriving. Only confirmed inbound before launch counts.
Wide routine diagram restructured into When/Then/Always lanes that wrap; the narrow vertical view is unchanged.
Holds all wording for the Today view, built from card fields with nothing hardcoded.
Focus view with approve flow, source sheet and done screen; the email review dialog was added here and Undo was removed for sent emails.

workflow: Use a one-time subagent for bulk cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans) and keep each builder on separate files to avoid edit conflicts.
Ask before paid API calls (e.g. the image recognizer run) and before pushing; the user approved the one cheap reading.
Check the actual rendered UI with screenshots on mocked data and view-only checks on live data, never clicking approve on real data.
A designer subagent producing target images first, then a single builder implementing, let the user reject cluttered directions cheaply.

friction: Portal token was empty at first, blocking the data pull until the user supplied it.
The first design canvas directions were judged way too cluttered, forcing a redo with a radical-reduction brief.
The UI showed Undo for emails that had already gone out, which was misleading, and phone Approve with no cost sends a real supplier email immediately with no preview.
Dashboard stayed at 34,800 locally because no shipping advice reading existed until a paid OpenAI run was approved.
The Teams header replacement missed a multi-line emoji header and needed a manual fix.
The Standard stop time was attributed to the wrong card, needing a tie-breaker fix.
Farhan was asleep, so the verifier fix had to be made without them and left with a note.
Unclear whether portal data and supplier interactions are the same for every team.
